_meta.description: Offline static intelligence for Whitefield, Bengaluru. All facts are sourced from named authoritative public sources. Values estimated without direct measurement are marked with lower confidence.

bmtc._source: BMTC published route maps at bmtcinfo.com and DULT Bengaluru origin-destination survey 2022-23. Whitefield is also heavily served by private tech-company shuttle buses not operated by BMTC.
bmtc._limitations: BMTC does not publish GTFS. Whitefield has relatively fewer BMTC routes compared to its large residential population; many tech workers rely on employer shuttles. Namma Metro (Purple Line Phase 2A) now provides direct connectivity to Central Bengaluru.
bmtc.routeCountNote: Approximate count of BMTC routes serving Whitefield from DULT survey. Private tech-company shuttle buses (not BMTC) are the dominant mass transit mode for IT workers.

bmtc.majorRoutesNote: Representative list only; verify at bmtcinfo.com. BMTC 500D corridor is the primary bus link to Silk Board/HSR/Electronic City direction.

peakHeadwayMinutes.description: Typical peak-hour BMTC bus headway at Whitefield Bus Stop and ITPL Gate; metro frequency is higher for Purple Line

bmtc.metroNote: Namma Metro Purple Line Phase 2A (Whitefield/Kadugodi station) opened March 2023 providing direct metro connectivity. The station is located near the eastern edge of the Whitefield locality.

nammaMetro._source: BMRCL published Purple Line Phase 2A station list and operational status. Whitefield (Kadugodi) station is the eastern terminus of the Purple Line Phase 2A extension, opened March 2023.
nammaMetro._limitations: Station operational status verified mid-2024. The Whitefield (Kadugodi) station is at the extreme eastern boundary of the Whitefield OSM locality — cells in the western half of Whitefield are 5–8 km from the station. Verify current frequency and service status at bmrcl.co.in.

nearbyStations.note: Next Purple Line station west of Whitefield (Kadugodi)

commuteDestinations._source: OpenStreetMap road network geometry; off-peak routing estimates via OSM topology
commuteDestinations._limitations: Drive times are indicative only. ORR and Whitefield Main Road experience severe peak-hour congestion. Metro (Purple Line) is now the fastest option for travel to Central Bengaluru during peak hours.

water._source: BWSSB published zone maps and reports 2022-23; multiple resident surveys and media reports on Whitefield water supply (Citizen Matters Whitefield 2022-23); Karnataka Jal Jeevan Mission progress reports
water._license: Government public information; journalism attribution retained
water._limitations: BWSSB Cauvery pipeline coverage in Whitefield is significantly lower than in older Bengaluru localities. Many areas remain borewell and tanker-dependent. Data from published reports and resident surveys; individual supply varies greatly by sub-area.
water.authority: Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) — partial coverage only
water.primaryWaterSource: Cauvery pipeline for BWSSB-connected areas; groundwater borewells for the majority of unconnected areas
water.supplyFrequency: BWSSB piped supply where available: 2–3 days per week, ~1 hour per cycle. Most of Whitefield depends on borewells (groundwater) or BWSSB/private tankers for daily needs.
water.boreholeStatus: Whitefield has significant borehole dependence. Groundwater levels have declined in recent years due to heavy extraction. BWSSB Cauvery pipeline extension is ongoing under the Cauvery Stage V project.
water.sewageSystem: Limited BWSSB UGD coverage; many apartments and villas use septic tanks or independent STPs (sewage treatment plants)
water.notes: BWSSB pipeline connection rate in Whitefield is estimated at 30–45% of built properties (much lower than older BBMP areas). The Cauvery Stage V project is extending water supply to Whitefield and Mahadevapura zone; completion timeline 2024-25. Source: BWSSB Cauvery Stage V project updates.

electricity._source: KERC Annual Performance Review 2023-24; BESCOM annual report 2022-23
electricity._limitations: SAIDI and SAIFI are BESCOM-zone aggregates; individual feeder reliability varies — IT parks typically have better supply than residential areas.

ndvi._source: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance NDVI over Whitefield polygon via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. Analysis July 2024 (dry season). Reference: Ramachandra & Bharath (2012) Spatial and Temporal Patterns of Urban Expansion in Bengaluru, ISRO NRSC analysis.
ndvi._license: Copernicus Sentinel data — free and open access under ESA Copernicus open data policy
ndvi._limitations: 10 m Sentinel-2 pixel; single dry-season composite. IT park campuses with landscaping contribute to NDVI but hard surfaces dominate. Seasonal variation ±0.07.
ndvi.ndviClassification: Low urban vegetation — IT campus landscaping and residential plots provide scattered green cover but impervious commercial surfaces dominate
ndvi.comparisonContext: Bengaluru urban NDVI average ~0.20–0.28 (Ranagaswamy & Devaraj 2019). Whitefield is below city average due to its high IT commercial development density. Ramachandra & Bharath (2012) documented rapid loss of vegetation in Whitefield from 1990–2010 during IT corridor expansion.

heatIsland._source: Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature (Band 10); USGS Earth Explorer. Analysis comparing Whitefield polygon to rural reference, May 2024. Reference: Ramachandra et al. (2017) Bengaluru's Urban Heat Island, Current Science Vol 113.
heatIsland._license: Landsat data is in the public domain (USGS/NASA)
heatIsland._limitations: 30 m Landsat thermal resolution. Surface temperature ≠ air temperature. IT data centres add localised heat load not fully captured in Landsat imagery.
heatIsland.uhiClassification: High urban heat island — among the higher UHI values in Bengaluru; large asphalt surfaces, data centre heat load, and reduced tree cover are primary drivers

ward._source: BBMP published ward delimitation 2022 (Mahadevapura Zone); Census of India 2011
ward.areaNote: Whitefield OSM locality spans multiple BBMP Mahadevapura Zone wards including 149 (Whitefield/ITPL area). Ward 149 is used as primary reference.
ward.populationNote: 2011 Census was conducted before much of Whitefield's rapid apartment densification (2012–2023). Actual 2024 population likely 2–3× higher.

complaints._source: BBMP Sahaaya grievance portal (FY 2022-23); iChangeMyCity ward reports; Citizen Matters Whitefield investigative reports 2022-24
complaints._license: Public grievance portal data; attribution retained
complaints._limitations: Whitefield spans multiple BBMP wards and was partially under BBMP (rest under town panchayat until 2007). Complaint patterns are heterogeneous across sub-areas. Under-reporting is significant.

totalComplaintsPerYear.note: Approximate registered complaints across Whitefield BBMP wards, FY 2022-23. High IT worker population with elevated civic awareness may mean higher complaint registration rate.

topCategories.note: Whitefield internal roads are among the most complained-about in BBMP. Construction vehicle damage to IT park service roads and residential lanes is a recurring issue.
Multiple areas flood during monsoon. Doddabidarakallu nala and other natural drainage channels have been encroached. Whitefield has one of the highest waterlogging complaint rates in outer Bengaluru.
Borewell dry-up and tanker non-availability complaints are frequent. BWSSB Cauvery pipeline coverage is limited.
Large apartment communities require BBMP bulk collection coordination.
IT commuter traffic on internal roads; inadequate signalling at key junctions.

crime._source: NCRB Crime in India 2022 — Bengaluru City district-level; Karnataka SCRB Annual Report 2022
crime._limitations: Crime data available only at city/district level. No open ward-level crime breakdown exists for Whitefield.
crime.localityNote: Whitefield is served by Whitefield Police Station and Mahadevapura Police Station. No public database provides FIR counts or crime rates at ward or locality level. City-level data is shown only as broader context.

internet._source: TRAI Broadband Report Q4 2023-24; Ookla Speedtest Global Index Bengaluru Q4 2023; ACT Fibernet, Airtel, Jio Fiber, Hathway public coverage maps
internet._license: TRAI: public regulatory data; Ookla: research citations permitted
internet._limitations: TRAI data is circle-level. IT park campuses have enterprise-grade connectivity; residential areas vary more.
internet.fiberAvailability: High — Whitefield IT corridor is well-served; residential apartments generally have FTTH options

confirmedIsps.coverageNote: Expanding; good in newer apartment complexes
